title: This Beetle Gets Eaten by a Frog, Then Crawls Out Alive

scenes.text: This beetle gets swallowed whole by a frog. Then it walks away.
It's a tiny water beetle, Regimbartia attenuata, only four to five millimeters long.
Researchers in Japan fed them to frogs. About 93 percent came out the other end within six hours, still alive.
The fastest escape took just six minutes.
Its secret is its legs. When researchers waxed them down, every beetle died.
A frog's stomach is no match for six kicking legs.

description:
A water beetle swallowed by a frog can escape alive, and about 93 percent did in a lab test.
Its legs make the difference: beetles with waxed legs all died.
Would you trust your legs against a frog's stomach?
first_comment: Frog or beetle: who would you bet on? Drop your weirdest escape story.
